title: Labor Market Signals Over Scores: BLS Update
discussion_signal: The post argues that one month of payrolls or unemployment can obscure labor-market friction, and recommends reading participation, hours, wages, and durable demand together. The audience reaction reinforces a preference for trend and multi-indicator interpretation over a single headline score.
linked_research_question: How do headline employment indicators differ from the lived stability, opportunity, and bargaining conditions experienced by workers?
limits: This is professional commentary rather than a representative worker sample
One post cannot establish labor-market causality
The interpretation may selectively emphasize friction indicators
